description: We are MioraX, a passionate team using technology, software, and data to solve real-world problems. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to tackle “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” Our interests span web dev, UI/UX, AI/ML, GIS, and data analysis. We welcome teammates in agriculture, climate, mapping, or software who are eager to learn, collaborate, and build solutions for the future of farming.
summary:
OrbitDrop is an intelligent agro-climatology dispatch engine engineered for smallholder farmers and irrigation managers in tropical dry zones (demonstrated in Sri Lanka's Mahaweli and cascade tank networks).

By integrating NASA POWER satellite agroclimatology feeds (solar radiation ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, air temperature T2M, relative humidity RH2M, wind speed WS2M, and precipitation PRECTOTCORR) with FAO-56 Penman-Monteith crop evapotranspiration models and Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) agronomy, OrbitDrop calculates precise, liter-accurate crop water deficits. It downscales regional satellite moisture data into high-resolution 30-meter micro-stress grids across farmer-drawn polygon parcels, preventing over-irrigation. With an automated 48-hour predictive rainfall lockout and a live dispatch controller, OrbitDrop conserves up to 35% of reservoir water, cuts pumping electricity costs, and preserves soil aeration.
details:
What Exactly Does It Do?

OrbitDrop replaces guesswork in agricultural irrigation with satellite-driven precision. Farmers or irrigation officers draw their field parcel boundary directly onto a high-resolution Esri satellite basemap. The system instantly ingests real-time NASA Earth Observation data for that exact coordinate centroid and computes:

1. Reference Evapotranspiration (ETo) using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation.

2. Crop-specific daily thirst (ETc) tailored to phenological stages (e.g., Rice/Paddy soaking, tillering, panicle initiation/flowering; Maize; Tomato; Sugarcane).

3. 30-meter micro-stress satellite downscaling that pinpoints critical dry spots, low-moisture zones, and saturated patches across the field.

4. Exact pump runtimes tailored to water delivery hardware (Drip 90%, Overhead Sprinkler 75%, Furrow 60%, Flood/Basin 50%) and pump flow rates (LPM / GPM).

5. 48-hour Predictive Rain Lockout that suspends pumping when rain is imminent, protecting both water reservoirs and crop root health.

How Does It Work?

Agro-Climatology Pipeline: Queries NASA POWER daily agroclimatology APIs for solar flux, surface temperatures, humidity, wind velocity, and rainfall.

Precision Agronomy Math: Evaluates thermodynamic net crop water demand (ETc = ETo × Kc) factored against soil root zone infiltration depth.

Micro-Stress Grid Engine:Simulates 30m spatial downscaling to detect localized water stress within the parcel boundary, visualizing AWD moisture thresholds: Red (<16% critical deficit), Amber (16-24% moderate stress), Green (>24% optimal).

Live Irrigation Controller:A real-time dispatch dashboard featuring a continuous pump simulation with accumulating liters, live map spray ripples, and an exportable 7-day agronomic prescription plan.

Benefits & Real-World Impact

Water Conservation:Saves up to 1.13+ acre-feet of reservoir water per field cycle by stopping unnecessary irrigation before rainfall.

Economic Relief: Reduces rural pumping fuel and electricity bills by hundreds of kilowatt-hours (kWh).

Climate Resilience: Implements AWD to curb anaerobic methane emissions from waterlogged paddy fields while securing yields against flash droughts.

Technologies & Software Stack

Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons.

Mapping & Geodata: Leaflet, Geoman.io Free (polygon drawing), Turf.js (geodesic area & centroid calculation), Esri World Imagery basemap.

Backend & APIs: Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB Atlas (field & telemetry persistence).

Data & Standards: NASA POWER API, FAO-56 Irrigation and Drainage Paper guidelines, Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture AWD practices.
